Sthala Purana & The Goddess

Shri Tulja Bhavani Mata

Tulja Bhavani is a form of Adi Parashakti, the divine Mother, widely worshipped as a family deity (Kuladevi) who protects and fulfils the wishes of her devotees.

Sthala Purana

As told in the Skanda Purana, Anubhuti, wife of the sage Kardama, performed penance on the banks of the Mandakini, seeking the Mother's protection for her infant child after the sage's death. When the demon Kukura tried to disturb her penance, Bhavani appeared and slew him, and from then on the Goddess is known as Tulja Bhavani. This is the legend of the original seat at Tuljapur; Peddamunigal's own story begins in the early 1900s (see Timeline).

Iconography & Attributes

The Goddess is shown with many arms holding weapons, riding a lion, as the slayer of Mahishasura. [Add your temple's specific details.]

The Bhagath Family (Priests)

Kethavath Jeevan Bhagawath is the sixth priest in the family lineage, serving since 1997 after his father Chandu Bhagawath. The Bhagath family performs the daily prayers to Mata Bhavani.

Temple Story

Read each card, then slide to the next →

1 / 10
🔱
The Mother

Mata Tulja Bhavani

A form of Adi Parashakti, worshipped as Kuladevi by countless families. She protects her devotees and destroys evil.

2 / 10
⚔️
Royal Devotee

Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj

Tulja Bhavani was the family deity of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Tradition holds that the Mother blessed him with the sword 'Bhavani Talwar' and watched over his Swarajya. He is remembered as one of her greatest devotees.

3 / 10
🌙
1850

The Dream

According to the priest, Goddess Bhavani appeared in an ancestor's dream and told him to fast through Navaratri for the well-being of the tribal people. The nine-day fast has continued since 1850.

4 / 10
🛖
Early 1900s

The Cloth Hut

Villagers began worshipping Bhavani in a small hut made of cloth, called 'paal' in the Lambadi language.

5 / 10
🤝
A Family Chosen

The Bhagath Family

Kethavath Hema Saukaar and the villagers appointed a family to serve the Goddess. The priesthood has since passed down the Kethavath family, generation to generation.

6 / 10
🛕
Mid-1950s

The Temple is Built

Kethavath Chandru Naik built the temple with the help of villagers and people from nearby villages.

7 / 10
🌊
1967

The Temple Stood

When the Nagarjunasagar reservoir was filled in 1967, Pedda Munigal village went under water, yet the temple remained standing. Water even entered the sanctum sanctorum.

8 / 10
🙏
1997

A Young Priest

After his father Chandu Bhagawath passed away, Kethavath Jeevan Bhagawath left his Class 10 studies to take up the priesthood in 1997. He is the sixth priest in the family lineage.

9 / 10
🥛
Every Dasara

The Nine-Day Fast

The priest keeps a strict fast through Navaratri, reportedly only a cup of milk in the morning and evening, while continuing the daily pujas.

10 / 10
🎉
Today

A Sea of Devotees

On Dasara, more than one lakh devotees, mainly Lambada (Banjara) tribals from Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, gather to worship the Mother.

Devotee of the Mother: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj

Jai Bhavani! Jai Shivaji!

Tulja Bhavani was the kuladevata (family deity) of the Bhonsle family. Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj worshipped the Mother with deep devotion, drew courage from her blessings, and is remembered as one of her greatest followers.

⚔️ The Bhavani TalwarTradition says the Goddess blessed him with his sword, known as Bhavani Talwar.
🚩 Protector of SwarajyaDevotees believe the Mother stood as protector of his Swarajya and of dharma.
🛕 At TuljapurHe is remembered for worshipping at the Tuljapur temple, the original seat of the Goddess.
